title: Pool Cost Sherpa + Thermocline Autoscale — compact controls for dedicated capacity
creator: Mateo Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, single-pane control surface for Dedicated GPU pools that combines cost visibility with autoscaling controls. The feature — internally dubbed 'Cost Sherpa with Thermocline' — should help platform engineers and SREs rapidly tune burst/autoscale thresholds while seeing immediate estimated cost and SLA impact. The goal is to reduce configuration mistakes, shorten ops feedback loops during incidents, and provide a responsive, keyboard-friendly micro-ui usable in narrow sidebars and full canvas views.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype in Figma covering sidebar and full-canvas variants
Interaction spec detailing autoscale slider behavior, burst presets, and keyboard shortcuts
Micro copy and inline help for cost estimates that ties to tokenized billing model
Accessibility checklist validated (keyboard nav, color contrast, screen reader labels)
Design handoff artifacts and annotated redlines for ENG-2741 and ENG-3012
comments: 2025-01-28 - Mateo Chen: Kickoff — sketched two approaches: (A) compact sidebar widget with condensed metrics and a single autoscale slider; (B) full-canvas thermocline panel showing percentile-based SLO bands and per-burst cost projection. Favor A for quick tuning, B as deep-dive.

2025-02-03 - Aisha Patel: Iteration 1 uploaded to Figma. Added inline 'impact preview' that overlays estimated monthly cost and SLA risk for each preset. Needs clearer distinction between 'burst' credits and steady autoscale targets.

2025-02-10 - Reviewed with PM (Ruth Delgado) — product wants explicit guardrails: default presets that map to contract tiers (dev, standard, enterprise) and a 'safety net' toggle that enforces fallback model variants under capacity pressure. Add copy for legal/SLA mapping.

2025-02-14 - UX research (Sana Rao): Ran 6 moderated sessions with platform engineers. Key findings: users liked immediate cost delta feedback but wanted a 'what-if' replay showing historical burst events applied to the new policy. Action: add a 7-day simulation toggle to the mockups.

2025-02-18 - Design review with Engineering (ENG-2741 owners): Discussed feasibility of live cost estimates. ENG requests a batching debounce (200ms) and an API flag to request 'estimate-only' calculations; otherwise risk pressure on control plane during rapid slider movement. Will add a minimal network interaction spec.
2025-02-22 - Accessibility review: color ramp adjusted; range input labelled and ARIA attributes planned; ensure tooltips dismiss on escape. Add alt layout for narrow widths (>320px).

2025-02-25 - PM approval (Ruth Delgado): Agreed on MVP scope: sidebar compact widget + full-canvas details view; simulation toggle deferred to stretch goal if backend estimate endpoint (ENG-3012) isn't prioritized this cycle.
2025-02-27 - Prototype QA: Links to two interactive flows created. Noted small polish items: slider thumb size, animation easing on cost-flip, and copy for the 'apply' confirmation.
2025-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Submitted final Figma files and redlines. Ready for engineering handoff; scheduling a 60-minute walkthrough with ENG-2741 and ENG-3012 on 2025-03-04.
decisions: Ship compact sidebar widget as the primary control surface for MVP to minimize surface area and reduce dev effort.
Expose three default presets (Dev / Balanced / Enterprise) mapped to reserve sizes and burst quotas; allow custom presets saved per pool.
Cost estimates will be 'best-effort' and use an 'estimate-only' API endpoint to avoid heavy load during interactive tuning (debounced to 200ms).
Simulation of historical events pushed to stretch (requires ENG-3012); MVP will surface 24-hour aggregated burst summary instead.
Accessibility and keyboard-first behavior are required for GA.
tradeoffs: Interactive live estimates vs control plane load: opted for debounced estimate-only API to balance UX and backend cost.
Compact vs expressive UI: chose compact MVP to speed rollout; richer thermocline visualization deferred to full-canvas view.
Preset guardrails increase safety but reduce flexibility; we provide a 'custom' mode with explicit warnings and a confirmation flow to mitigate risk.
implementation_notes: ENG needs a new endpoint GET /pools/:id/estimate?policy=preview that returns delta_cost and delta_latency percentiles (ENG-3012).
Design tokens: use existing token group 'charts.spectral.thermocline' for percentile bands. If not available, fall back to 'charts.spectral.neutral' and request token addition.
Define telemetry events: policy.preview, policy.apply, preset.select, simulation.toggle — include pool_id and actor_id.
Handoff package includes: Figma file, redlines PDF, component spec (range input, preset chips, micro-metric chip), copy deck, and acceptance criteria checklist.
next_steps: 2025-03-04: Walkthrough with ENG-2741 & ENG-3012 — confirm API contract and debouncing behavior.
Coordinate with Research to schedule follow-up 5-user unmoderated test for final microcopy check.
Prepare Atlassian/Confluence handoff doc and link to QA checklist; tag SRE and Security for review.
If ENG-3012 ready, iterate on 7-day simulation visualization in parallel as a stretch goal.
